doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lester Young's originality, bandmates and nicknames
summary: Pres created language and style, reminded him of Monk, and nicknamed Shorts McConnell and Ted Briscoe the Religious Brothers.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So you spent a time with Pres. Pres must have been – in ’47 Pres was – that was the cat. He created the languages. He had the dress. He . . .
He was original all the way round, I thought. Monk reminded me a lot of Lester Young.
Who else was in the band?

Shorts McConnell, playing trumpet. On bass was – oh boy. I forget. I ccould see him. The bass player, he used to go to the Catholic Church, and Shorts McConnell. Shorts used to hit all the high notes with Bill Eckstine and Earl Hines. Then he had sort of lost his chops. It was there, but it wasn’t the same as it used to be. They used to go to church a lot, the bass player – Briscoe – Ted Briscoe, from Washington, D.C., and Lester Young nicknamed them the Religious Brothers. He had a nickname for everybody. He’d say, “You two are Religious Brothers.”
What was the nickname he had for you?
Not too much. He used to call me the Royal of Haynes. I didn’t hear him have any other titles for me.
